0.content: "A Lonely Place" (also: A Lonely Place): "A Lonely Place" is a named subarea in the northern zone of Elynas, the colossal dead beast whose remains form much of the Beryl Region of Fontaine. It is where the Traveler sets out in the Ancient Colors quest "Limner, Dreamer, and Robotic Dog" to follow Jakob toward the heart of Elynas, and it is also the area listed for the world quest "The Lone Phantom Sail".

1.content: "A Very Bright Place" (also: A Very Bright Place): "A Very Bright Place" is a half-submerged cavern inside the southern zone of Elynas, the vast dead beast whose remains shape Fontaine's Beryl Region. Its walls hold many ore veins and it is filled with a congealed orange substance. The young Melusine Puca likes to collect pretty stones here, which is how the world quest "Strange Stone Chronicle" begins.

2.content: "A Very Warm Place" (also: A Very Warm Place, Elynas' heart, Scenery Within Elynas' Depths): "A Very Warm Place" is the name of the spot where Elynas' heart lies. Elynas is the huge dead creature whose remains fill Fontaine's Beryl Region and shelter the Melusines. The heart is why the air there is warm. When the Traveler first reaches it, it lies dormant under a layer of crystallized stone.

3.content:
Abandoned Production Zone (also: Abandoned Production Area): The Abandoned Production Zone is a closed-off industrial level at the bottom of the Fortress of Meropide, Fontaine's underwater prison in the Liffey Region. A lift near the waypoint on the Production Zone's lower level leads down to it. Four passages (Supply Warehouse 1, Supply Warehouse 2, the Energy Storage Warehouse and the Geode Mine Shaft) branch from a central chamber and are opened or shut by a large gear-driven drive valve. Notes left lying around show the fortress's daily life: petty complaints, makeshift experiments and boredom.

Status as of 7.1: Sealed and quiet as of 7.1, with Camden on watch. No later content changes it.

4.content: Alain Guillotin's Resting Place (also: Alain's grave, Alain Guillotin's grave): A small cave in Fontaine, just north of Chemin de L'Espoir and a little above the entrance to Annapausis, holds the grave of Alain Guillotin, the founding director of the Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering and creator of Sandrone. It is reached through the story quest "Those We Have Kept" in the Sunny Summer Fontinalia event, and stays open afterwards.

5.content:
Alta Semita (also: High Pathway, Golden Aqueduct): Alta Semita (Latin, roughly "High Pathway") is the golden aqueduct system of Capitolium, the inner city of Remuria, sunk in the Sea of Bygone Eras off Fontaine. It once carried Ichor out from the Domus Aurea toward "the great lake in the far north", and from above it looks like a giant harp. After millennia it had broken apart. In the quest Gradus ad Capitolium the Traveler and the dragon Scylla rebuild it so that the gates of the Domus Aurea will open.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the aqueduct stands rebuilt after the 4.6 quests. No later content revisits it.

6.content:
Annapausis: Annapausis is a flooded, hushed area in the Court of Fontaine Region, unlocked during the world quest The Narzissenkreuz Adventure. It lies where the Narzissenkreuz Institute, a Fontaine orphanage, once stood, and it is the setting in which the small Oceanid Ann leads the "Narzissenkreuz Adventure Team". The whole place has the feel of a story played out in a dream.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Annapausis remains a submerged, dreamlike place in the Court of Fontaine Region; no later change to it is recorded in the sources checked.

7.content:
Aquanigma (also: Sinthe production base): Aquanigma is the hidden headquarters of Vacher's Sinthe operation, reached by diving beneath Salacia Plain in Fontaine. In it the Traveler and Paimon found the factory where Sinthe was mixed and the laboratory where Vacher dissolved people in Primordial Seawater. It exists in game only as a quest domain during the Archon Quest "When All Return to the Waters".

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 canon gives no further use of the base. After Vacher's arrest the Sinthe production line was stopped and authorities moved to seize remaining stock.

8.content:
Beaumont Workshop (also: Atelier Beaumont): Beaumont Workshop is a blacksmith's shop in the Vasari Passage of the Court of Fontaine, owned by Estelle. Its map description calls it the most renowned forging workshop in the Court.

Status as of 7.1: Open as a shop at the cutoff (7.1); nothing in later content changes it.

9.content:
Belleau Region (also: Belleau): The Belleau Region is the western part of Fontaine's map. It holds Poisson, a fishing town built in an old ship and a cavern below sea level, which is the main base of the Spina di Rosula; Romaritime Harbor, a waterfall elevator and lookout where Fontaine's aquabus line meets the way to Sumeru; and the western slopes of Mont Automnequi. In the Archon Quest it is where the Primordial Seawater disaster strikes Poisson.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Poisson is recovering from the Primordial Seawater disaster and no later content has changed the region.

10.content:
Bertin's House of Curiosities (also: Bertin's House): Bertin's House of Curiosities is a shop in Quartier Lyonnais of the Court of Fontaine, run by Mequignon. It sells curios such as jewels, instruments, perfumes and souvenirs, yet is technically a fashion workshop.

Status as of 7.1: Open at the cutoff (7.1).

11.content:
Beryl Region (also: Beryl): The Beryl Region is a mountainous area in southern Fontaine, across the water from the Court of Fontaine. Its ridges and ruins are said to be what is left of a colossal beast, Elynas. Beneath its lakes lies Merusea Village, the home of the Melusines, and in the waters between the ridge and Mont Automnequi lies the Elton Trench, where Fontaine's old Navy sank.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Elynas' remains still shape the area and the Melusines of Merusea live there.

12.content:
Bravais' Press Works (also: Bravais Press Works, Bravais' Press Workshop, Arkhium Forge): Bravais' Press Works is a hidden underground workshop in the Submerged Stony Path below the Liffey Region of Fontaine. Its big Forging Press refines Arkhium Stock (fused from seven Mysterious Ores) into Arkhium Lumenite. Running the press ends with the whole chamber flooding, so it can be used only once. Its paperwork mentions a Senior Researcher named Bravais, whom nobody else seems to care about.

Status as of 7.1: After the Arkhium Lumenite is collected the press is flooded and ruined; the workshop remains submerged. Nothing newer than 4.1 is recorded.

13.content:
Caesareum Palace (also: Caesareum, Palace of Caesareum): Caesareum Palace is a ruin in Machimos, the outer city of Remuria's drowned capital. It served as a training ground for the empire's legions and as the place where the chains meant to bind the vishap prince Scylla were stored. According to the records, the Harmost Boethius ordered Legio VI to hold the Dragonborn back here, and the legion defended it to the end.

History: When Scylla marched Dragonborn on the capital, the Harmost Boethius gave Legio VI Rithimi Versi the task of stopping them here. The legion defended the palace until the end, with not a single deserter and no enemy breaking through, according to ancient records.

Status as of 7.1: Quiet after the Requiem. The area is explorable and its dead legionaries are at rest.

14.content:
Café Lutece (also: Cafe Lutece): Café Lutece is a well-known coffee house in the Vasari Passage of the Court of Fontaine. The wiki calls it the main restaurant for Fontaine. Arouet manages it. Its map description calls it the most popular café in the passage and says that the owner encourages customers from every background to discuss philosophy and other subjects as they drink their coffee. Any topic is allowed except death.

Status as of 7.1: Open and operating as of 7.1, as far as the sources show.

key: Central Laboratory of the Fontaine Research Institute
15.content:
Central Laboratory Ruins (also: Ruins of the Central Laboratory, Central Laboratory of the Fontaine Research Institute, Fontaine Research Institute ruins): The Central Laboratory Ruins are what remains of the heart of the old Fontaine Research Institute, in the Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering Region next to the Liffey Region. Years before the Traveler arrived, an experiment built around the crystal Arkhium exploded here and destroyed most of the Institute. The wreckage now hangs in a distorted gravity state beside large cubes of water floating in the air, and the surviving researchers treat it as a hazard that could blow again.

History: The Institute's Arkhium Research Project aimed to use Arkhium, a powerful crystal energy source, to counter gravity and perhaps lift Fontaine into a "city in the sky" so people could survive the prophesied flood. An overload of the project's Arkhium Kinetic Core caused a huge explosion that destroyed most of the Institute and left the Central Laboratory in ruins.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the ruins are stable but dangerous, kept under watch by the Institute, and the Arkhium is inert. No later version is known to have changed them.

16.content:
Chemin de L'Espoir (also: Path of Hope): Chemin de L'Espoir (French for "Path of Hope") is a subarea in the Court of Fontaine Region of Fontaine, within the map level of the Source of All Waters, the Great Fontaine Lake. It is known in canon mainly as a place on the map and as the starting point of a timed Daily Commission. No story or lore is tied to it.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is an ordinary, accessible part of Fontaine's capital region with no recorded events.

17.content: Chevalmarin Film Fantasyland (also: Fantasyland): Chevalmarin Film Fantasyland is an amusement park and fan convention for film lovers in the Court of Fontaine Region. It was the idea of the engineer Lepine-Pauline and was built almost overnight by Navia and the Spina di Rosula for the limited-time Whirling Waltz event in Version 5.6. Its theme is Fontaine's film-making, and it is named for Surintendante Chevalmarin, whose image Lepine-Pauline was allowed to use by Furina.

18.content:
Chioriya Boutique (also: Chioriya): Chioriya Boutique is a fashion shop and label owned by Chiori, an independent designer from Inazuma, on a busy street in the Quartier Lyonnais of the Court of Fontaine. It looks small, but passers-by stop to look in, and its clothes have a good reputation. Its owner has a blunt, lightning-quick manner with troublemakers. The wiki also records a nickname for it, the 'intelligence boutique', because customers talk freely about their business there.

Status as of 7.1: Open and trading as of 7.1, as far as the sources show.

19.content:
Clivus Capitolinus (also: Capitoline Hill, Capitoline Rise): Clivus Capitolinus is the hill at the heart of Capitolium, the inner city of ancient Remuria's capital. Its summit holds the Domus Aurea, the royal palace. The name also covers the cavern under the hill, which contains the Local Legend Cineas, called the Unreturned Envoy. It is named after the road up the Capitoline Hill in Rome.

History: This was the centre of Remuria: the palace where Remus listened to every note of the empire and corrected any discord with a pluck of his strings, surrounded by theatres and palaces with carved beams and domes. After the great wave, the whole hill sank.

Status as of 7.1: Quiet since the Requiem. The Domus Aurea above is silent and Cineas remains in the cavern, where he can be fought but need not be.

20.content:
Collegium Phonascorum (also: College of Music Teachers, Court of Harmonious Rhythm): The Collegium Phonascorum (Latin, roughly "college of music teachers") was the educational centre of Remuria, set in the inner city Capitolium under the sea off Fontaine. There the Harmosts and music lecturers taught Remurians about the symphony of Phobos. Notes left among its ruins record a Harmost's reasoning about music, will and fate, and show how a learned institution fed a brutal ideology.

Status as of 7.1: Ruined and silent as of 7.1, a sunken place whose lessons now serve only as record.

21.content:
Coupon Cafeteria (also: Meropide cafeteria): The Coupon Cafeteria is the canteen of the Fortress of Meropide, in its Administrative Area, where convicts gather for daily meals. Each prisoner may claim one free Welfare Meal a day from the clockwork meka Bran.

Status as of 7.1: Operating at the cutoff (7.1).

22.content:
Court of Fontaine (also: City of the Arts, Cour de Fontaine): The Court of Fontaine is the capital of Fontaine, a Belle Epoque-style city of fountains, cobbled avenues, boutiques, cafes and theatres standing high above the surrounding waters. It was once the court of the God of Justice; since the events of the Archon Quest "Masquerade of the Guilty" (4.2) it has been under Chief Justice Neuvillette, who runs the nation from the Palais Mermonia at the city's summit. The Steambird, a newspaper read across Teyvat, is based here, and the city is nicknamed the "City of the Arts".

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Court of Fontaine is at peace. Fontaine has no Hydro Archon; Chief Justice Neuvillette administers the nation from the Palais Mermonia and judges trials himself now that the Oratrice no longer works. Furina has left the Palais and lives in the city as an ordinary human and actress.

23.content:
Court of Fontaine Region (also: Court Region): The Court of Fontaine Region is the central map area of Fontaine. It holds the capital, the Court of Fontaine, where justice is a public spectacle; the open waters of Salacia Plain; the sunken Institute of Natural Philosophy; the hidden Annapausis; and the Opera Epiclese courthouse on the island of Erinnyes.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Court of Fontaine Region is intact and in everyday use.

key: Court of Fontaine Aquabus Main Station
24.content:
Court Region Waterway Hub (also: Court of Fontaine Aquabus Main Station, Aquabus Main Station): The Court Region Waterway Hub is the aquabus main station in the centre of the Court of Fontaine. It serves the Clementine Line to Romaritime Harbor, the Navia Line to the Opera Epiclese and Marcotte Station, and the Callas Line to the Fontaine Research Institute.

Status as of 7.1: Active at the cutoff (7.1) with two lines running.

25.content:
Damoville Purveyor: Damoville Purveyor is a general goods shop in the Vasari Passage of the Court of Fontaine, run by Boucicaut.

Status as of 7.1: Open at the cutoff (7.1).

26.content:
Denouement of Sin: Denouement of Sin is a Domain of Blessing in the Belleau Region of Fontaine, near Romaritime Harbor. In the domain text it is a remote, deserted valley where legend says the first Lochknight hid among the Lochfolk, training harshly in an attempt to atone for a sin beyond redemption. Now only cold wind blows and clockwork meka left without orders still patrol.

Status as of 7.1: Accessible as a permanent artifact domain as of 7.1; no story events are tied to it.

27.content:
Domus Aurea (also: The Domus Aurea, Golden Palace of Remuria, royal palace of Remuria): Domus Aurea ("Golden House") was the royal palace of the kingdom of Remuria. King Remus, the Sebastos and God King, had it made from his ship Fortuna and designed it as a giant instrument on which the Grand Symphony, Phobos, could be played. It is the "heart" of Phobos and is protected by that power. It lies on the hill of Clivus Capitolinus in Capitolium, deep in the Sea of Bygone Eras, and looks strangely well preserved for something thousands of years sunk.

History: Remus took Sybilla's wisdom and his own power to make Phobos, which would let humanity take charge of its own fate against the prophesied destruction. The palace was its stage. Phobos took on a will built from the worst desires of the ascended Remurians, who had put their souls into immortal golem bodies, and it led them into war on the other peoples of Fontaine. Remus tried to end it with a secret Requiem, a self-destruct order for the symphony, to be carried out with Scylla; Scylla was lured into a trap and sealed, and the Requiem sank Remuria in a flood.

Status as of 7.1: Quiet after the Requiem. Phobos is gone for good, the souls it held have left, and the people of Petrichor are back to normal.

28.content: Dryas Wood (also: Dryas Pine Forest): Dryas Wood is a small hollow in Fontaine between the Fontaine Research Institute and Erinnyes Forest. It used to be the Institute's "backyard", where plant nurseries stood, and it is said that the potioneer who devised the "Pure Water" formula once lived here in seclusion. It is now abandoned.

29.content:
East Slopes of Mont Automnequi (also: Mont Automnequi East): The East Slopes of Mont Automnequi are the eastern side of Mont Automnequi, a mountain in Fontaine that spans two regions. This half belongs to the Morte Region; the western half is in the Belleau Region. It was added in Version 4.2.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is an accessible slope with its ruin and quest content unchanged.

30.content:
Echoes of the Deep Tides: Echoes of the Deep Tides is a weapon-material domain of underwater caves in the Court of Fontaine Region. Bandits and smugglers use the caves, beyond the Maison Gardiennage patrol routes, as hideouts, and have stolen clockwork meka. Its flavor text recalls a God King who dreamed of an empire of harmonious music above the waves, whose pride sank with him.

Status as of 7.1: A permanent weapon domain as of 7.1; no story events are tied to it.

31.content:
Elton Trench (also: Graveyard of Ships): Elton Trench is a deep underwater trench in Fontaine, in the Beryl Region between the beast-mountain of Elynas and Mont Automnequi. It is the final resting place of the old Fontaine Navy, which sank here fighting the great beast Elynas about 500 years ago. Its water is oddly bright, so divers misjudge its depth, yet the shipwrecks littering its bottom warn them off; local legends call the nearby waters haunted, which also makes it a good hiding place for anyone who wants secrecy.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the trench is a silent graveyard; no recent event has changed it.

32.content:
Erinnyes Forest: Erinnyes Forest is a green, lake-filled area on the island of Erinnyes in Fontaine. Its landmarks are the Weeping Willow of the Lake, the Roots of Erinnyes (the water veins whose centre is called Hauteclaire), the lake Loch Urania and Lumidouce Harbor, a port built on a waterfall. The world-quest series The Wild Fairy of Erinnyes deals with cleansing its polluted waters.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the willow and lake are healthy again after the Wild Fairy of Erinnyes quests.

33.content:
Faded Castle (also: The Faded Castle, golden castellum): The Faded Castle is a sunken ruin in the Nostoi Region that was once part of ancient Remuria. The Harmosts and scholars of Remuria lived there, maintaining archives and researching music theory and fate. The castle holds the portal to the Sea of Bygone Eras, an even deeper region where the main Remurian ruins lie. The Traveler first enters it during the 4.6 World Quest The Shadow Over Petrichor.

History: In Remuria's golden age the Harmosts kept records of plays, scores and stories here. After the empire fell, Boethius gathered the survivors of Remuria into the castle as the Golden Troupe to resurrect the dead empire. Cassiodor opposed him, because the plan meant destroying the new nation of Fontaine and stealing its people's souls, and sealed the passage to the surface.

Status as of 7.1: The castle is now open. The seal is gone, and Phobos has been silenced, so the portal leads to quiet ruins.

34.content:
Faded Theater: Faded Theater is an artifact domain in Petrichor, in the Nostoi Region of Fontaine. Its flavor text says that the prophet and the ruler, heroes and fell dragons, the grand opera of the golden age once played out here; now the only players on the stage are monsters of unknown provenance.

Status as of 7.1: A permanent artifact domain as of 7.1, added in 4.6; no story events are tied to it.

35.content:
Fleuve Cendre (also: Court of Fontaine: Fleuve Cendre, Ashen River, Fleuve cendré, the undercity of Fontaine): Fleuve Cendre ("Ashen River") is the undercity of Fontaine: a damp, poorly lit settlement in the sewers beneath the Court of Fontaine. Societal outcasts live here: ex-convicts, active criminals, the destitute, orphans and manual labourers whom the surface no longer needs. The Court of Fontaine has long treated it as a grey legal area outside its jurisdiction. Today the Spina di Rosula, led by Navia, is its de facto government.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Fleuve Cendre remains a poor, damp undercity under the Spina di Rosula's watch. No later canon changes its state.

36.content:
Foggy Forest Path (also: Foggy Forest Path subarea): The Foggy Forest Path is a subarea in the southern part of Erinnyes Forest, by the water, where mist hangs among the trees and a glowing blue tree stands out. It is the setting of the world quest "Foggy Forest Path", part of "The Wild Fairy of Erinnyes", added in Version 4.2.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the area is unchanged and accessible.

37.content:
Fontaine (also: Nation of Justice, Fontainian): Fontaine is the nation of Hydro and justice, a "terrestrial sea" on a raised plateau at the centre of Teyvat, said to be the source of all the continent's waters. Its capital, the Court of Fontaine, is a Belle Epoque-style city of fountains, aquabuses, clockwork meka and theatres, and Fontainians pride themselves on art, elegance and technology. Trials at the Opera Epiclese are public spectacle. Since 4.2 Fontaine has had no Archon: the Iudex Neuvillette, secretly the Hydro Dragon, runs its affairs.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Fontaine is at peace and has no Archon. In 4.2 the real Hydro Archon, Focalors, executed herself through the Oratrice, destroying the Hydro Archon's throne; Neuvillette regained the Hydro Dragon's authority and absolved Fontainians, who no longer dissolve in Primordial Seawater. Furina abdicated and now lives as an ordinary actress and director. Neuvillette runs the nation and judges trials himself.

key: Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering Region
38.comment: Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering Region
38.content:
Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering Region (also: Kinetic Energy Engineering Region): This is the area where the Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering stands. Years ago the Institute's central laboratory was largely destroyed in an explosion linked to Edwin Eastinghouse's research into Arkhium, leaving huge Allogravity-Condensed Water Bodies floating in the air. The organisation now works from a nearby New Fontaine Research Institute.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the old laboratories remain in ruins and the Institute operates from the New location.

39.content:
Forbidden Zone: The Forbidden Zone is the hidden lowest part of the Fortress of Meropide, Fontaine's undersea prison. It is built over Primordial Water, and a giant sluice gate there was made to stop that water from flooding Fontaine. Only the Fortress's Administrator, Wriothesley, may enter, and he reaches it by a secret stair from his office.

Status as of 7.1: Its sluice gate was resealed by Neuvillette in 4.1.

40.content:
Fort Charybdis Ruins (also: Fort Charybdis, Mysterious Ruins of Fort Charybdis): Fort Charybdis Ruins are the remains of a fort on an island in the eastern part of the Morte Region. Inside lies a hidden underground complex, the Orthant of Wishes, which holds one of the four Seals of Chymical Marriage placed by the Narzissenkreuz Ordo. The fort's name is also spoken by Remurian golems in 4.6 as a place where their legions were told to fall back. Canon text about the fort itself is thin.

History: No source describes who built the fort or why. The Ordo later used the site as one of four seals for its Great Ritual; the diary of a member records that the party found "Remuria's ruins" at the indicated location and arranged an official construction project.

Status as of 7.1: Unchanged since the 4.2 quest. The seal and the Ordo's apparatus remain.

41.content:
Fortress of Meropide (also: Meropide): The Fortress of Meropide is a metal-walled stronghold under the sea in Fontaine's Liffey Region. It serves as Fontaine's de facto prison: people convicted at trial are sent there to serve their sentences. It is also the nation's largest maker of clockwork meka. Legally it governs itself. Convicts there count as exiles, and the Court of Fontaine has no jurisdiction beyond lending some Gardes for security. Inside, Credit Coupons replace Mora. The Administrator is Wriothesley, a former inmate who holds the honorary title of "Duke". The Melusine Sigewinne runs the infirmary.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Fortress still operates as prison and factory under Wriothesley, with Sigewinne as Head Nurse.

42.content: Fountain of Lucine (also: Fontaine de Lucine, Lucine Fountain): The Fountain of Lucine stands in front of the Opera Epiclese in the Court of Fontaine. Fontainians say all of the nation's water ultimately gathers there, and it is the origin of the habit of tossing coins into fountains to make wishes. It has listened to Fontainians' wishes for a very long time.

43.content: Genesis of a Certain Micro-Universe (also: The World's Amniotic Fluid): Genesis of a Certain Micro-Universe is a stretch of the Primordial Sea, the ancient water beneath Fontaine, reached only during the world quest Waking from the Great Dream (4.2). It is the arena where the Traveler, Paimon and Ann face Narzissenkreuz, the failed leader of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo.

44.content: Geode Mine Shaft (also: Arkhium Crystal Geode Mine Shaft): The Geode Mine Shaft is an abandoned mine in the Fortress of Meropide's abandoned production zone, filled with Arkhium crystal and patrolled by Flying Energy Thieves. It is the escape route used in the world quest An Eye for an Eye.

45.content:
Hidden Dwelling (also: Guillotin home): The Hidden Dwelling is the former home of Alain Guillotin and of his creations Sandrone and Pulonia. Its map description calls it a place where flowers and grasses flourish and time passes gently. It is a quiet house that bears witness to everything that unfolded in the 'home'. It becomes accessible in the 6.7 event story Those We Have Lost and stays open afterwards.

Status as of 7.1: Quiet and open to visit as of 7.1.

46.content:
Hortus Euergetis: Hortus Euergetis (Latin, "Garden of Euergetis") is an underwater garden in Machimos, the outer city of Remuria in the Sea of Bygone Eras. It takes its name from Euergetia, a Harmost of Remuria who died in the kingdom's destruction. A short engraving at its waypoint, signed by Ouranides of Ouranopolis, wishes her peace and promises that flowers will always bloom for her here.

Status as of 7.1: A quiet sunken memorial as of 7.1; nothing in later content changes it.

47.content:
Hotel Bouffes d'ete (also: Hôtel Bouffes d'été, Hotel Bouffes d'été, the Hotel): Hotel Bouffes d'ete is a luxurious hotel in the Vasari Passage of the Court of Fontaine. It is legally owned by the Fatui Harbinger Arlecchino, called 'Father' by the orphans there, and is the base of her House of the Hearth in Fontaine. A children's home runs behind the hotel front. Lyney, Lynette and Freminet live there.

Status as of 7.1: The House of the Hearth's Fontaine base, with Arlecchino as owner, as far as the sources read.

48.content:
Hotel Debord (also: Debord, Debord restaurant): Hotel Debord is a famous restaurant in Quartier Narbonnais of the Court of Fontaine. Its owner, Vaneigem, holds that art is the best seasoning for good food and often invites performers to entertain diners.

Status as of 7.1: Open at the cutoff (7.1) under Savanna's management.

key: Entrance of the Passage of Ianus
49.content:
Initium Iani (also: Entrance of the Passage of Ianus): Initium Iani (Latin, roughly "the beginning of Ianus") is the great gate between Machimos, Remuria's outer city, and Capitolium, its inner city. It leads to the Passage of Ianus, the only way between the two, and it was where the dragon Scylla was sealed. In The Last Day of Remuria, Scylla, freed after millennia, blasts it open so the Traveler, Paimon and Monsieur Os can reach the Domus Aurea.

Status as of 7.1: Broken open by Scylla during the 4.6 quests; the door swung shut behind the group. No later content revisits it.

50.content:
Institute of Natural Philosophy (also: The Institute of Natural Philosophy, Submerged Ruins of the Institute, Liliacruces Forum ruins): The Institute of Natural Philosophy is a dilapidated underwater research facility that once belonged to an organisation of the same name led by Director Dwight Lasker. Much of its research is still preserved in the flooded ruin, including precursors of modern Fontainian technologies and the earliest experiments of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo. The Traveler first reaches it in the Version 4.0 World Quest Aqueous Tidemarks.

History: The Institute was a research body led by Dwight Lasker. During a cataclysm about five hundred years ago Dwight closed it for the safety of its people and kept the young from going to fight, urging post-disaster reconstruction first.

Status as of 7.1: Still flooded and abandoned. Its documents remain, and its oldest dangers are guarded by meka.

51.content:
Lepaute Horlogerie: Lepaute Horlogerie is a clock shop in Quartier Lyonnais, owned by Caron. Horlogerie is French for clockmaking, and the shop stands near his older brother Livre's toy workshop.

Status as of 7.1: Open at the cutoff (7.1).

52.content:
Leschots Clockwork Workshop (also: Leschots's workshop, Leschots Clockwork Shop): Leschots Clockwork Workshop is a toy shop in Quartier Lyonnais run by Livre, who makes mechanical clockwork toys.

Status as of 7.1: Open at the cutoff (7.1).

53.content:
Liffey Region (also: Liffey): The Liffey Region is the part of Fontaine's map that holds the Fortress of Meropide, an underwater stronghold that serves as Fontaine's de facto prison and largest maker of Clockwork Meka. Its Administrator is Wriothesley, and the infirmary is run by Sigewinne. Foothills on the east side of Mont Esus also belong to the region.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Fortress still operates under Wriothesley and Sigewinne.

54.content: Loch Urania (also: Urania Lake): Loch Urania is a lake in Erinnyes Forest, Fontaine, containing a large water vortex that forms a big bubble at the top. It starts out tainted by contaminated bacterial mats; clearing them calms the water and the sky.

55.content:
Lumidouce Harbor (also: Port de Lumidouce): Lumidouce Harbor is a coastal elevator and observation deck built into the side of a waterfall in Fontaine's Erinnyes Forest, much like Romaritime Harbor. It is a vital trading port for Fontaine, handling a large volume of international cargo, including tea from Qiaoying Village in Liyue and spices from Sumeru. For some years it has been underfunded and worn down, with its planned expansion and aquabus line stalled.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Lumidouce Harbor is still a stagnant but working port. No later canon changes its state.

56.content:
Marcotte Station: Marcotte Station is the terminus of the aquabus Navia Line, serving the Erinnyes area.

Status as of 7.1: Active at the cutoff (7.1).

57.content: Mary-Ann Memorial Park: Mary-Ann Memorial Park is a small, once scenic park just south of the Central Laboratory Ruins, in the area of Fontaine given over to the Fontaine Research Institute. Most of its buildings were destroyed by the explosion that levelled the old Institute. Beneath its shallow pond lies Bossuet's Abandoned Laboratory.

58.content:
Administrative Area (also: Meropide Administrative Area, Fortress of Meropide Administrative Area): The Administrative Area is the central hub of the Fortress of Meropide, the undersea prison-factory in Fontaine. The Duke's Office, belonging to the Administrator Wriothesley, stands at its centre. The Fortress's teleport waypoint is here, across from the office. Guards, inmates, shopkeepers and the doctor all pass through it.

Status as of 7.1: Active as of 7.1, with Wriothesley as Administrator.

59.content:
Production Zone (also: Meropide Production Zone, Fortress of Meropide Production Zone): The Production Zone is the work area of the Fortress of Meropide. It has two levels below the Administrative Area, joined by a lift in the east of the Fortress. Inmates work here, and further below, through a lift in the lower level, lies the Abandoned Production Zone.

Status as of 7.1: Operating as the Fortress's factory floor as of 7.1.

60.content:
Merusea Village (also: home of the Melusines, Melusine village): Merusea Village is the home of the Melusines, the small amphibious all-female people of Fontaine. It lies underwater, inside the body of the dead beast Elynas, and the game calls it "an adorable and mysterious village where even the chimneys bubble". It has no official leader. Very few humans ever visit, but those who do tend to enjoy it.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Merusea Village remains a hidden, peaceful Melusine home with no leader. No later canon changes its state.

61.content:
Mont Automnequi (also: Mont Automnéqui, Automnequi): Mont Automnequi is one of Fontaine's most iconic peaks, a mountain that straddles two regions: its west slopes lie in the Belleau Region and its east slopes in the Morte Region. Much of Fontaine is covered by water, but this is one of the places where mountain and forest show through. From its heights one can look across to the ridge of Elynas and the lakes beneath which the Melusines' homeland is hidden.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 nothing new has been reported on the mountain; it remains accessible and quiet.

62.content:
Mont Esus (also: Esus): Mont Esus is a very large mountain in Fontaine, north-west of the Court of Fontaine. It appears in the in-game expedition menu but cannot be visited. What players can see is its foothills by the sea close to Palais Mermonia, a gentle landscape of wide flower fields, and its eastern foothills, which form the Mont Esus East subarea.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Mont Esus is still a distant, inaccessible peak. Nothing in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content changed that.

63.content:
Mont Esus East (also: East Foothills of Mont Esus): Mont Esus East is the eastern foothills of Mont Esus in the Liffey Region of Fontaine. Mont Esus itself is a huge mountain north-west of the Court of Fontaine that the player cannot reach, so these foothills are the part that can be explored. The area came with Version 4.1.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the foothills are accessible, while Mont Esus itself stays out of reach.

64.content:
Morte Region (also: Morte): The Morte Region is the eastern waters of Fontaine's map. Its centrepiece is the Tower of Ipsissimus, also called the Sealed Ruined Tower or the Tower of Gestalt, built by the Narzissenkreuz Ordo as its base. The area also has Fort Charybdis Ruins on an island, the east slopes of Mont Automnequi, four Orthants and, reached through the story, a place called the Genesis of a Certain Micro-Universe in the Primordial Sea.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tower is permanently submerged and the Ordo story is complete.

65.content:
New Fontaine Research Institute (also: The New Fontaine Research Institute, Alain Guillotin Research Institute): The New Fontaine Research Institute is where the Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering works now. It was built near the ruins of the Central Laboratory after the Arkhium explosion there. Before the disaster the Institute was known as the Alain Guillotin Research Institute and hosted weekly lectures about critical projects. Its staff here include a Material Collation team, a fish-type clockwork meka research team and a Fonta vending machine.

Status as of 7.1: The Institute's working headquarters as of 7.1.

66.content:
Northland Bank (Fontaine) (also: Banque du Nord, Northland Bank Court of Fontaine): The Northland Bank in the Court of Fontaine is a branch of the Snezhnayan Northland Bank, in Quartier Lyonnais. Its sign is written in Fontaine Script as BANQUE DU NORD.

Status as of 7.1: Present at the cutoff (7.1); its interior remains inaccessible.

67.content:
Nostoi Region (also: Nostoi): The Nostoi Region is a southern island area of Fontaine that sits outside the raised continental plate the rest of the nation stands on, so the waters around it cannot be dived into. It contains Petrichor, a beautiful town known for very pure water and a view of the great waterfall that rings Fontaine, and the sunken Faded Castle, an old Remurian ruin that leads down to the Sea of Bygone Eras.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Petrichor is peaceful and the castle's secrets have been opened up.

68.content:
Opera Epiclese: The Opera Epiclese is a grand opera house on the island of Erinnyes in the Court of Fontaine Region, and also Fontaine's main courthouse. Trials are held on its stage as public performances before a ticketed audience, with the Iudex Neuvillette presiding from a raised seat. On other nights the same stage hosts plays, musicals, concerts and magic shows. Behind the opera house a lift descends to River Talionis, the wharf from which convicts are shipped to the Fortress of Meropide.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Opera Epiclese still hosts both trials and performances, with Neuvillette as presiding judge.

69.content:
Orthant of Memory (also: Hall of Memory, Room of Memory, Memory Orthant): The Orthant of Memory is one of four Seals of Chymical Marriage in the Morte Region of Fontaine, set by the Narzissenkreuz Ordo. Its riddle slate announces "the Orthant of Memory, the Hall of Memory, the Room of Memory" and the answer to its riddle is a shadow. The Memory piece it once held, one of four substances for forging the Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz, was already gone when the Traveler arrived; the quest Muse's Mother covers it.

Status as of 7.1: Opened and emptied; the Memory piece is gone. Nothing newer than 4.2 is recorded.

70.content:
Orthant of Persona (also: Persona Orthant): The Orthant of Persona is the last of the four Seals of Chymical Marriage left by the Narzissenkreuz Ordo in the Morte Region of Fontaine. Its riddle ends with "the first droplet", and the answer that opens it is an Oceanid. It holds the Persona piece, the most important of the four substances for forging the Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz, which Jakob wants and which Caterpillar gives the Traveler to keep.

Status as of 7.1: Open; the Persona piece is in the Traveler's hands. Nothing newer than 4.2 is recorded.

71.content:
Orthant of Souls (also: Shrine of Souls, Room of Souls, Souls Orthant): The Orthant of Souls is one of the four Seals of Chymical Marriage set by the Narzissenkreuz Ordo, placed in Mysterious Ruins on the east slopes of Mont Automnequi in the Morte Region of Fontaine. Its riddle slate names it "the Orthant of Souls, the Shrine of Souls, the Room of Souls", and the answer to its riddle is love. By the time the Traveler arrives the Soul piece has already been removed. The quest is Cupid's Lover.

Status as of 7.1: Opened and emptied. Nothing newer than 4.2 is recorded.

72.content:
Orthant of Wishes (also: Temple of Wishes, Room of Wishes, Wishes Orthant): The Orthant of Wishes is one of the four Seals of Chymical Marriage left by the Narzissenkreuz Ordo, hidden in the Mysterious Ruins of the Fort Charybdis Ruins in the Morte Region of Fontaine. Its slate calls it "the Orthant of Wishes, the Temple of Wishes, the Room of Wishes", and the riddle's answer is life. The Wish piece it held was already taken when the Traveler came; the quest is Meteoric Lance. On the second floor an Ordo member's diary records the Great Ritual.

Status as of 7.1: Opened and emptied. Nothing newer than 4.2 is recorded.

73.content:
Palais Mermonia: The Palais Mermonia stands at the highest point of the Court of Fontaine and is where all of Fontaine's administration is handled. To Fontainians it is effectively the highest authority in the land. It houses Iudex Neuvillette's office and the government bodies called Maisons: Ordalie (the judiciary), Gestion (administration and documents), Cardinalice (financial approvals) and Gardiennage (law enforcement), along with the Marechaussee Phantom. It was also Furina's residence while she reigned as Hydro Archon. She moved out after 4.2.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Palais Mermonia remains the seat of Fontaine's government, with Neuvillette handling the nation's affairs from his office there.

74.content:
Pale Forgotten Glory: Pale Forgotten Glory is a talent-material domain: the submerged wreckage of a once-proud ship on the seabed north-east of Poisson, in Salacia Plain. What should have been a quiet final resting place is full of mysterious creatures.

Status as of 7.1: A permanent talent domain as of 7.1; no story events are tied to it.

75.content: Pankration Ring (also: Pankration Arena): The Pankration Ring is the arena of the Fortress of Meropide, the underwater prison of Fontaine. Pankration, a bare-fisted combat sport, is the Fortress's most popular entertainment. The host, Roussimoff, announces bouts from the platform above the stage.

76.content:
Passage of Ianus (also: Ianus Passage): The Passage of Ianus is an underwater corridor in the drowned city of Remuria (Fontaine). It joins the outer city, Machimos, to the inner city, Capitolium.

Status as of 7.1: Submerged and ruined, still the way between Machimos and Capitolium.

77.content:
Petrichor (also: Petrichor town, the Musicmaking Town): Petrichor is a picturesque town on an island in the south of Fontaine, off the continental plate that carries the rest of the nation. It is known for its beauty and its exceedingly pure waters, and is a popular spot for viewing the great waterfall that encircles Fontaine. A council of elders, the Consilium Sapientium, governs it by tradition, with a "Doge" as its head. Its mountains hold ruins and stone golems from the ancient kingdom of Remuria.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Petrichor is a calm island town ruled by the Consilium Sapientium, with its Remurian ruins quiet. No later canon changes its state.

78.content:
Poisson (also: Poisson village): Poisson ("fish" in French) is a fishing village in the Belleau Region, at the foot of Mont Automnequi and built from a great ship and a large cavern below sea level. Its people mostly fish or salvage from underwater. It is the headquarters of the Spina di Rosula and Navia's home ground. In 4.2 an earthquake near Poisson sent Primordial Seawater flooding through the lower town, killing twelve people; it has since been rebuilt with Fatui help.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Poisson has been rebuilt after the 4.2 flood and remains the Spina di Rosula's headquarters. No later canon changes its state.

79.content: Poisson Tunnel (also: The Poisson Tunnel): The Poisson Tunnel is the passage carved through the West Slopes of Mont Automnequi so that the Clementine aquabus line can run beneath the mountain, between the Court of Fontaine and Romaritime Harbor. The Fontaine Research Institute dug it with newly built engineering machines, including the "Golden Vessel".

80.content:
Portus Anticus (also: Where Only the Bell Tolls): Portus Anticus was the royal port of Remuria. It has since sunk into an underwater cavern, part of the Sea of Bygone Eras in Fontaine.

Status as of 7.1: A sunken, ruined port that can be explored.

81.content:
Quartier Lyonnais (also: Court of Fontaine: Quartier Lyonnais): Quartier Lyonnais is a street of shops along the northeastern side of the Court of Fontaine. The Fontaine branch of the Adventurers' Guild is here, alongside clockmakers, a boutique and a shop of curiosities.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 no change to the district is recorded; it remains an ordinary shopping street.

82.content:
Quartier Narbonnais (also: Court of Fontaine: Quartier Narbonnais): Quartier Narbonnais lies on the southwestern side of the Court of Fontaine. It is home to The Steambird, the city's main newspaper, and to Hotel Debord, a famous restaurant, and it is considered a place to find the newest fashion and perfume.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 no change to the district is recorded.

83.content:
Rag and Bone Shop: The Rag and Bone Shop is a small shop in the Administrative Area of the Fortress of Meropide, Fontaine's undersea prison. Its owner, Alvard, sells all sorts of goods to inmates, who pay in Credit Coupons, a currency used only inside the fortress.

Status as of 7.1: Open and operating as of Version 7.1.

84.content:
Remuria (also: Kingdom of Remuria, Empire of Remuria, Pax Remuria, Eternal City, Undersea Capital): Remuria was the empire of the god Remus, who called himself the God King and was known to his people as the Sebastos or Imperator. He founded it on the waters of what is now Fontaine, before the Hydro Archon Egeria ruled. It prospered on music and art, its capital was Capitolium, and its emblem was a golden bee. It was prophesied to face utter destruction, and Remus's attempts to avoid that destiny wrecked it. It drowned in a single catastrophe and now lies in the Sea of Bygone Eras.

History: After the first civilisation fell to flood, Fontaine had no real civilisation for a very long age. Remus arrived in his ship and brought agriculture, cities and music. Seers prophesied that his empire would be utterly destroyed, so he built the Grand Symphony, Phobos, and put the souls of his people into immortal bodies to escape fate. Phobos magnified the cruellest wishes of the ascended Remurians, they went to war with the other peoples of Fontaine, and in the end a tsunami drowned the empire.

Status as of 7.1: Only ruins, golems and memory remain. In Version 4.6, Phobos was finally ended and its souls went to the sea; Remuria is no longer a threat.

85.content: Rift of Erosion: The Rift of Erosion is a point of interest in the Fortress of Meropide, west of the Dormitory Block in the Administrative Area. It is called a "potential danger" and is guarded by Galvana.

86.content: River Talionis: River Talionis is a small wharf beneath the Opera Epiclese in the Court of Fontaine, the external reception area of the Fortress of Meropide. A single boat carries prisoners through an underground tunnel straight to the Fortress.

87.content:
Romaritime Harbor (also: Romaritime Station): Romaritime Harbor is a large coastal elevator and observation deck built into a waterfall on Fontaine's edge. A lift carries people between the harbor below and the top of the falls, where the Clementine Line aquabus runs on rails to the Court of Fontaine. It is also the way to the Girdle of the Sands in Sumeru, and Aeval calls Romaritime Station "one of the great gateways of Fontaine".

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Romaritime Harbor is a working port and aquabus terminus. No later canon changes its state.

88.content:
Roots of Erinnyes (also: Depths of Erinnyes, Hauteclaire): The Roots of Erinnyes are a network of subterranean caverns and water veins beneath the island of Erinnyes in Fontaine, in the region of Erinnyes Forest. Its waters work as an information system, and the central part is called Hauteclaire. Many of its channels lead up to the Weeping Willow of the Lake. In the 4.2 world quest series The Wild Fairy of Erinnyes, the Traveler cleanses it of corruption alongside a strange Melusine named Pahsiv.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the roots are cleansed and healthy. The willow is vibrant blue, and no later content has changed the area.

89.content:
Sacellum Requietis (also: The Sacellum Requietis, throne room of Domus Aurea): The Sacellum Requietis is the throne room of Domus Aurea, the royal palace of Remuria. The God King Remus once ruled from it. In Version 4.6 it is where the Traveler silences the Grand Symphony Phobos at the end of the Canticles of Harmony quest chain.

History: The room is where Remus held court. According to the old book on Remuria, the king rested at the heart of the palace, listening to every melody and note from across the empire and correcting any discord with a pluck of his strings. He used that position to guide his people's symphony.

Status as of 7.1: Peaceful since the Requiem. Phobos is gone and the palace is silent.

90.content:
Salacia Plain: Salacia Plain is an open, serene stretch of crystal-clear sea in the Court of Fontaine Region. It is explored with the blessing of the Transoceanic Sourcewater, which lets travellers pass here unhindered, and it is home to sea creatures such as the Angelic Sea Hares and the singing Blubberbeasts.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 no change to the area is recorded.

91.content:
Salon Caritat: Salon Caritat is a society in the Quartier Narbonnais of the Court of Fontaine devoted to the study of law and the improvement of justice. In practice its members act like a civic advocacy group, currently pressing on government spending and water pollution.

Status as of 7.1: Active as of Version 7.1, with members still voicing concerns around the Court of Fontaine.

92.content:
Sea of Bygone Eras (also: Undersea Capital): The Sea of Bygone Eras is a stretch of Fontaine's waters, too deep for sunlight to reach, where the capital of ancient Remuria lies in ruins on the sea floor. It is reached through the sunken Faded Castle in the Nostoi Region and has its own map. Its ruins include the warrior city Machimos, the gated inner city Capitolium and, on the hill at its heart, the golden palace Domus Aurea, where the God King Remus once tended the "symphony" that ruled his empire.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the sunken capital is quiet: Phobos was destroyed in 4.6, the trapped Remurian souls have passed on and Scylla is free in the deep.

93.content:
Secret Vault (also: Marechaussee Hunter vault): The Secret Vault is a hidden vault in the Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering Region, with its entrance east of the Central Laboratory Ruins. It holds a stone tablet of past Marechaussee Hunters' names and deeds, and some old weapons.

Status as of 7.1: Opened; the tablet and weapons remain.

key: Memories: The Titan Amidst the Stars
94.content:
Shadow of Another World (also: Memories: The Titan Amidst the Stars): Shadow of Another World is a Trounce Domain in Salacia Plain, Fontaine, unlocked after completing the Archon Quest "Finale". It lets the Traveler relive the battle against the All-Devouring Narwhal, the beast from another world. Its flavor text says that battle was the intersection of this world's fate, that Fontaine now treads a brighter path, and that the giant's whale-song will not fade from memory.

Status as of 7.1: A permanent boss domain as of 7.1, added in 4.2; no new story events occur in it.

95.content:
Thalatta Submarine Canyon (also: Thalatta Canyon): The Thalatta Submarine Canyon is an underwater subarea of the Court of Fontaine Region, within the map level of the Source of All Waters, the Great Fontaine Lake. Its name uses "Thalatta", the Attic Greek form of the word for sea. It debuted in Version 4.0.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is accessible and has no known story events.

96.content: The Duke's Office (also: Duke's Office, Wriothesley's office): The Duke's Office is Wriothesley's office, in the centre of the Administrative Area of the Fortress of Meropide. Its door is often shut tight, yet its owner knows everything that happens in the Fortress. It has three floors.

97.content: The Narzissenkreuz Ordo (also: Narzissenkreuz Ordo chamber): The Narzissenkreuz Ordo, as a place, is the hidden meeting chamber of the secret society of the same name. It sits at the top of the Tower of Ipsissimus in Fontaine. In its ceiling is a Doomsday Clock made by the mage Narzissenkreuz to count down to the apocalypse of the Prophecy of Fontaine.

98.content: "The Real Annapausis" (also: The Real Annapausis): "The Real Annapausis" is the hidden heart of Annapausis, reached after Ann's storybook quest to rescue Princess Lyris. It is where the consciousness of Mary-Ann, a hybrid Oceanid, resides. First entered in the world quest "Mary-Ann's Story" (4.0), it then closed until "Rowboat's Wake" (4.2) made it permanently accessible.

99.content:
The Wingalet (also: Wingalet, Wingalet Gloop-Gloop Funderwater Fisharium): The Wingalet is a very large ship that Wriothesley, administrator of the Fortress of Meropide, built in secret in the Forbidden Zone beneath the prison. He began it once he suspected the Primordial Sea lay just beyond the Fortress's sluice gate, meaning it as an escape vessel and something for Fontainians to hold on to. It surfaced during the Prophecy of Fontaine to rescue people from the flood, then went back into storage. In Version 6.7 it was leased out during the Fontinalia Film Festival and fitted with an aquarium.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Wingalet belongs to the Fortress of Meropide and, since 6.7, doubles as an aquarium that Wriothesley agreed to keep running in part.

100.content:
Tower of Ipsissimus (also: Tower of Gestalt, Sealed Ruined Tower): The Tower of Ipsissimus, also called the Tower of Gestalt or the Sealed Ruined Tower, stands in Fontaine's Morte Region. The secret society known as the Narzissenkreuz Ordo built it as its base. The Court later declared the Ordo an illegal extremist group and sealed the site. The tower is the way down to a seal over the Primordial Sea, and it sinks beneath the water for good after the 4.2 world quest Savior's Wake.

Status as of 7.1: Sealed by the courts and, since 4.2, permanently submerged.

101.content:
Vasari Passage (also: Court of Fontaine: Vasari Passage): Vasari Passage sits at the bottom (south) of the Court of Fontaine. Streets lined with shops lead toward a large fountain plaza, and a cafe and several vendors serve passers-by.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 no change to the district is recorded.

102.content: Weeping Willow of the Lake (also: Erinnyes's Watery Weeping Willow, Saule pleureur du lac): The Weeping Willow of the Lake is a large willow growing at the centre of a lake in Erinnyes Forest, its roots apparently reaching under the water. Fontaine's lore treats it as a barometer: it flourishes or withers as the water veins run sweet or bitter.

103.content:
West Slopes of Mont Automnequi (also: Mont Automnequi West): The West Slopes of Mont Automnequi are the western side of one of Fontaine's most iconic peaks, in the Belleau Region; the east side lies in the Morte Region. The slopes are known for the Poisson Tunnel, which carries the Clementine Line through the mountain, and for the clockwork inventor Antoine. Added in Version 4.0.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the slopes are accessible and unchanged.
